datasets.card_excerpt: # Multi-ATS Job Postings Snapshot (June 2026) A dated snapshot of **112,816 job postings** collected from **23 different Applicant Tracking Systems** (Workday, Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, iCIMS, SmartRecruiters, Oracle Cloud, Workable, Paylocity, and more) and parsed into a clean, consistent 47-column schema with a large language model. Unlike typical single-source job dumps, every row is enriched with **extracted skills, salary ranges, qualifications, experience level, work model, and geocoded location (lat/lon)** — useful for salary modeling, skills-demand analysis, NLP, and labor-market research. Data sourced and structured by **[NextGig](https://www.nextgig.rocks)** — for live, current listings visit https://www.nextgig.rocks. ## Highlights - 112,816 postings · 13,412 companies · 23 ATS platforms · ~540 geo regions - 47 structured columns - ~51,800 postings (46%) include structured salary min/max - Skills extracted for ~71%; geocoded lat/lon for ~94% - LLM-generated role summaries (98%) ## Quick start ```python from datasets import load_dataset ds = load_dataset("NextGig-Rocks/global-job-postings-multi-ats", split="train") print(ds[0]) ``` List-type columns (`skills_required`, `minimum_qualifications`, etc.) are stored as JSON strings — parse with `json.loads`. ## What this is NOT A **point-in-time research snapshot**, not a live feed. It deliberately contains **no application URLs, no apply links, and no source identifiers** — it cannot be used to apply to jobs or to power a live job board. ## Known limitations - `date_posted` is sparse (~20%); not suitable for time-series/trend analysis. - `country`/`city` are derived from geocoded strings and are approximate. - The `job_description` field is an LLM-generated 2–4 sentence factual summary of the role (not the original posting text) and may contain occasional errors. - Some fields (e.g. `years_experience_numeric`, `equity`) are sparsely populated. ## License **CC BY 4.0** — free for commercial and non-commercial use **with attribution** to NextGig (https://www.nextgig.rocks).

datasets.card_excerpt: # Employer-direct job postings with source provenance **25,000 live job postings where every row states where it came from.** Static sample exported **24 October 2026** from Job Opportunities API (JOA). Collected from employers' own career pages, their ATS feeds and official government feeds. No job boards, no staffing agencies, no reposts. ## Why this sample exists Most job datasets come from scraping job boards. That gives you the same posting five times, rewritten by an agency, with a salary nobody published, and no way to tell which is which. JOA collects from the source and keeps the evidence. **Every row in this export carries its source class** (`source_type`), and `salary_published` is true only when the employer actually printed a number. Nothing is inferred and then presented as fact. If you want the live feed instead of a snapshot, with daily updates, delisting signals and a change feed across millions of postings, the API is at https://jobopportunitiesapi.org. The statistics endpoints work with no key at all. ## Fields | Field | Meaning | |---|---| | job_id | Stable JOA identifier | | title | Job title as published | | employer | Employer name | | employer_website | Employer's own domain, when known | | industry | Employer industry, when known | | country | ISO country code | | location | Location text as published | | employment_type | Full-time, part-time, contract, when published | | salary_min, salary_max | As published | | salary_currency, salary_period | Currency and period as published | | salary_published | true only if the employer printed a salary | | source_type | Source class: career_site, ats, or public_agency | | ingest_mode | How the row was collected | | first_seen_at, last_seen_at | When JOA first and last saw the posting live | | apply_url | Direct link to the employer's own apply page | | description | Posting text, truncated to 3,000 characters | ## What is deliberately not here - Rows without a known source class. This export keeps only rows whose provenance is recorded. - Rows where we could not open the apply page and confirm the posting is live. - Aggregator and job-board sources. JOA refuses those by name. - Inferred salaries. If the employer did not publish a number, the salary fields are null. ## Known limits This is a static export. Postings close, so some rows here are no longer live. The live API answers that question instead. Salary coverage reflects the market: most employers do not print a salary. ## License an

See `README_jobs.md` for the full data card (provenance, collection method, per-platform coverage caveats, license) and `SCHEMA_jobs.md` for the column dictionary. Fresh, scheduled data (including an incremental "posted within N days" mode for a daily sweep): the source Apify Actor at https://apify.com/make_no_mistakes/multi-ats-job-board-api Not sure which ATS a company runs on? The free companion Actor https://apify.com/make_no_mistakes/company-ats-detector resolves it for you. Source and templates (n8n, Make, Postman, MCP): https://github.com/makenomistakesllc/apify-actors --- # Tech Job Postings — 9 ATS Platforms (Sep 2026) ## What this is 7,516 open job postings pulled directly from 284 companies' career-site applicant-tracking systems, spanning all nine ATS platforms the `multi-ats-job-board-api` Apify Actor normalizes: Greenhouse, Ashby, Lever, Workday, SmartRecruiters, Recruitee, Rippling, Personio and Workable. Every posting is flattened onto one schema — title, department, team, location, remote flag, employment type, salary (where the platform publishes it), posted/updated dates, apply link and description — so postings can be compared across employers and platforms without hand-building nine separate scrapers. **Why it's useful.** Job postings are a real-time labor-market signal: which companies are hiring, into which functions, at what seniority, and (on the minority of platforms that publish it) at what pay. Most public job datasets only cover Greenhouse/Lever/Ashby-style startups because those three platforms are the easiest to scrape. This dataset deliberately also includes Workday (the ATS most large enterprises run on), SmartRecruiters, Rippling, Personio and Recruitee, so it demonstrates coverage across small-startup and large-enterprise hiring alike. ## Provenance Every row comes from a public, zero-authentication JSON or XML endpoint that the platform itself exposes to power the employer's own careers page — not a scrape of the rendered HTML page: | Platform | Public endpoint pattern | |---|---| | Greenhouse | `boards-api.greenhouse.io/v1/boards/{token}/jobs` | | Ashby | `api.ashbyhq.com/posting-api/job-board/{org}` | | Lever |

datasets.card_excerpt: # AI Job Postings in 12 Countries, October 2026 **Full page:** https://mariascales.com/research/ai-jobs/data/ 17,513 job postings from the US, the UK and ten more European countries, collected in October 2026. About four in ten carry AI in the title. Most of the others are ordinary roles from matching job families, collected as a comparison. For every posting I keep the title, the employer, the employer type and a set of flags computed from the full text: does it mention AI, does it ask for Python, does it talk about adoption and change management. The posting texts themselves are left out. I built it to answer one question: what does the word AI in a job title tell you? ## What is inside | file | what it is | |---|---| | `postings.csv` | 17,513 postings, one row each | | `employers.csv` | 7,173 employers with their type and how the type was set | | `summary_ai_mentions_in_comparison_roles.csv` | share of ordinary roles that mention AI, by country, region and employer type | | `summary_employer_mix.csv` | which employer types hire for AI roles, next to who hires for the comparison roles | | `summary_ai_role_vs_comparison.csv` | what an AI title adds: change management, Python, stakeholders, prompting, years of experience | | `summary_ai_depth.csv` | how many sentences of an ordinary posting mention AI, by employer type (English texts, non-engineering roles) | | `summary_about_us.csv` | how much of the AI in ordinary postings sits in the company description, by employer type | | `summary_country_language.csv` | ordinary roles that mention AI by country, in English and in the local language | The summary files are computed from `postings.csv`. You can rebuild every number from the postings file. ## Three numbers from this data * **The employer predicts AI in an ordinary job.** Among ordinary roles with an English text, AI comes up in **68%** of postings at tech companies (n=1,265), **49%** at consultancies (n=812) and **30%** everywhere else (n=1,896). datasets.card_excerpt: # Djinni Dataset (English Job Descriptions part) ## Overview The [Djinni Recruitment Dataset](https://github.com/Stereotypes-in-LLMs/recruitment-dataset) (English Job Descriptions part) contains 150,000 job descriptions and 230,000 anonymized candidate CVs, posted between 2020-2023 on the [Djinni](https://djinni.co/) IT job platform. The dataset includes samples in English and Ukrainian. The dataset contains various attributes related to job descriptions, including position titles, job descriptions, company names, experience requirements, keywords, English proficiency levels, publication dates, language of job descriptions, and unique identifiers. ## Intended Use The Djinni dataset is designed with versatility in mind, supporting a wide range of applications: - **Recommender Systems and Semantic Search:** It serves as a key resource for enhancing job recommendation engines and semantic search functionalities, making the job search process more intuitive and tailored to individual preferences. - **Advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs):** The dataset provides invaluable training data for both English and Ukrainian domain-specific LLMs. It is instrumental in improving the models' understanding and generation capabilities, particularly in specialized recruitment contexts. - **Fairness in AI-assisted Hiring:** By serving as a benchmark for AI fairness, the Djinni dataset helps mitigate biases in AI-assisted recruitment processes, promoting more equitable hiring practices. - **Recruitment Automation:** The dataset enables the development of tools for automated creation of resumes and job descriptions, streamlining the recruitment process. - **Market Analysis:** It offers insights into the dynamics of Ukraine's tech sector, including the impacts of conflicts, aiding in comprehensive market analysis. - **Trend Analysis and Topic Discovery:** The dataset facilitates modeling and classification for trend analysis and topic discovery within the tech industry. - **Strategic Planning:** By enabling the automatic identification of company domains, the dataset assists in strategic market planning. ## Load Dataset ```python from datasets import load_dataset data = load_dataset("lang-uk/recruitment-dataset-job-descriptions-english")['train'] ``` ## BibTeX entry and citation info *When publishing results based on this dataset please refer to:* ```bibtex @inproceedings{drushchak-romanyshyn-2024-introducing, title = "Introducing the Djinni Recruitment Dataset: A Corpus
